description_full: ZOZO, Inc. operates online shopping Websites in Japan. It operates ZOZOTOWN a fashion online shopping website that includes services, such as ZOZOUSED, a website for secondhand/vintage apparel; ZOZOCOSME, an online cosmetic store; ZOZOSHOES, a shoe-specialized zone; and ZOZOVILLA that brings together domestic and international brands. It also operates WEAR, an outfit-sharing app; ZOZOFIT, a 3D body scanning technology solution; ZOZOMO, and online merges offline platform that offers fulfillment support and reservation services; ZOZOMETRY that offers measurement process optimization service for businesses; ZOZOGLASS, a skin tone capturing device that solves customers' challenge of cosmetic product color selection; ZOZOMAT, a 3D feet measuring tool; ZOZOSUIT, a 3D body measurement service; and PayPay mall. In addition, it engages in the advertisement business. The company was formerly known as Start Today Co., Ltd. and changed its name to ZOZO, Inc. in October 2018. ZOZO, Inc. was incorporated in 1998 and is headquartered in Chiba, Japan. ZOZO, Inc. is a subsidiary of Z Intermediate Holdings Co.,Ltd.

financial_summary: ZOZO INC is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $6.3B market cap on $1.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 139% against a 9% cost of capital — a 130-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 93% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $285M in free cash flow — roughly 20 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.10× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 53% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 30% operating margin runs 23pp above the Consumer Cyclical median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 3.83x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 76% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 10% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 218% and a beta of 0.99, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y -2.96 vs 5y -12.15), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $51 a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 35% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $5.84 (margin of safety -26%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 23%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $4.79 to $7.34 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Consumer Cyclical peers: P/FCF 22.3 vs 16.7 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.5% (below the risk-free rate).
The price implies 7.8% annual cash-flow growth, 4pp more than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 139% clears the cost of capital of 9.5% by 130pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.14).
It runs a 93% gross margin and converts 20% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.10x.
ROE of 45% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $309.5M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 10.0, in the safe zone).
The Beneish M-score (-1.96) sits just under the manipulation line, so earnings quality bears watching.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 3.8% over 3 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
own: Insiders own 52.8%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 26%.
It returns 4.2% a year to shareholders (1.0% in buybacks and 3.4% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 12 consecutive years.
people: With about 1,894 employees, each generates about $755K of revenue, 2.0x the Consumer Cyclical median.
That works out to $150K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $569K (1x revenue per employee).
